headline: Iran claims three US F-35 fighter jets destroyed in Jordan attack
summary: The Middle East sees escalating conflict as Iran targets US bases in Kuwait and Jordan following US strikes in Iran.
details: The Middle East is facing a surge in conflict as the US and Iran engage in retaliatory strikes. Following a five-day lull, the US launched attacks on Iran on Wednesday night, resulting in casualties, including three civilians on Kish Island and three IRGC members in Janjan province.

In response, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targeted US military installations in Kuwait and Jordan. In Kuwait, attacks on the Ali Al-Salem base destroyed two drone hangars and a fuel tank, while a civilian building belonging to a Chinese company was hit, killing one worker.
The IRGC claims to have destroyed three US F-35 fighter jets and damaged three others during a missile strike on Jordan's Al-Azraq airbase. However, the US military has rejected these claims.

The conflict is expanding beyond the two nations, with Saudi Arabia joining the US in strikes against Iraq, and Houthi rebels targeting Saudi Arabia. Additionally, two ships were attacked in Egyptian ports, increasing tensions around the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab Strait.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has expressed deep concern over the widening conflict, warning that a return to diplomacy is urgent. This follows a series of failed ceasefires and a broken memorandum of understanding between the US and Iran.

US President Donald Trump had previously suggested that discussions were going well, but later told Fox News that Iran would receive 'hard punishment' before the latest strikes. The IRGC has vowed to continue defending Tehran as long as US threats persist.

headline_marked: Bangladesh Bank [[cuts policy rate to 9.50%]] to boost investment
headline: Bangladesh Bank cuts policy rate to 9.50% to boost investment
summary: The central bank reduced the repo rate by 50 basis points after 21 months to encourage private investment and create more jobs.
details: Bangladesh Bank has reduced the policy rate, or repo rate, from 10% to 9.50% to encourage investment and employment. This decision, made during the 13th meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), will take effect from August 2.

The move comes after 21 months of no changes to the policy rate. The central bank aims to lower loan interest rates for commercial banks, which is expected to lead to lower borrowing costs for customers and entrepreneurs.

According to the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS), private investment as a percentage of GDP was at its lowest in 14 years in the last fiscal year. This decline has been attributed to political uncertainty, economic crises, and a lack of business-friendly environments.
The central bank also reduced the Standing Lending Facility (SLF) rate from 11.50% to 11%, while the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) rate remains unchanged at 7.50%.

The decision was made after reviewing global and domestic inflation, private sector credit flow, and economic growth. While inflation remains high (above 9%), it has decreased slightly compared to previous periods.

The move is also intended to address stagnant employment, particularly among educated youth. BBS data shows that one in three graduates is unemployed, with approximately 9 lakh educated unemployed people in the country.
